evidence.record_quote: MIA contains the writings of close to 1000 authors representing a complete spectrum of political, philosophical, and scientific thought, generally spanning the past 200 years.

atoms.reference: Over 400,000 documents and 1.1 TB of data in 83 languages (April 2026).

evidence.record_quote: MIA contains these writings in 83 different languages , comprising a total size of over 400,000 documents and 1.1 TB of data (April 2026), all created through the work of volunteers around the world.

atoms.reference: To maintain an archive of any and all writings which are Marxist or relevant to the understanding of Marxism and can be lawfully published.

evidence.record_quote: The MIA aims to maintain an archive of any and all writings which are Marxist or relevant to the understanding of Marxism and can be lawfully published.

atoms.reference: A seven-tenet Charter (free, non-profit, democratic, full disclosure, politically independent, does not 'judge' writers, archival priority); the 2007 end of the Marxist/non-Marxist division; public domain unless noted.

evidence.record_quote: MIA abides by seven fundamental tenets found in our Charter : (1) We will always be 100% Free; (2) We will always be a non-profit organization; (3) We will always be based on democratic decision making; (4) We will always have full disclosure; (5) We will always remain politically independent; (6) We do not ‘judge’ writers; (7) Our priority is to provide archival information.
In 2007, we terminated our former practice of dividing all writers into Marxists and non-Marxists , and instead offer an index of Selected Marxist Writers in most language sections.
All material within these Archives, unless noted otherwise, is public domain . MIA-created material is protected by the Creative Commons License .

observations.notes: The library composed accurately at the level of its sections, with a count from an earlier state of the site. What it leaves out is the terms on which it holds: its charter's refusal to judge writers, which is what keeps the losing side of every split on its shelves.
